class: Any data-health rule that calls an instrument stale because its last tick or exchange timestamp is older than a fixed age misflags every quiet but current instrument on a feed that sends only changes, so a healthy chain shows a share of its contracts as stale at all times.
mechanism: Kite's WebSocket sends a packet only when a contract changes; far strikes stay unchanged for minutes while the connection is live. backend/ofo/marketdata/health.py marks a quote stale when its timestamp is older than stale_after (60 s).

first_seen.evidence: 09:15-09:45, feed never quiet for more than 0.51 s, yet a median 59 and max 354 of 1,091 contracts had no tick for over 60 s (staleness_timeline inst_stale_gt_60s); 99.5% of inter-tick intervals were 30 s or less

fix: Health follows the feed's state for the subscription (connected, subscribed, heartbeats and data frames arriving) and the contract's last-known value stays current while the feed is live; a contract's own age is shown as information, never as stale by itself. Decided in the data-path work item.

detection.note: A replay test over the recorded 2026-10-08 frames: with the feed live, no contract may be marked stale; with an inserted gap longer than the feed threshold, every contract must be.

occurrences.evidence: inst_stale_gt_60s median 59 of 1,091 with feed_stale false in all 360 samples
